params.name: pre_receive_environment_id
params.description: The unique identifier of the pre-receive environment.

items.docs:
If you attempt to delete an environment that cannot be deleted, you will receive a `422 Unprocessable Entity` response.

The possible error messages are:

*   _Cannot modify or delete the default environment_
*   _Cannot delete environment that has hooks_
*   _Cannot delete environment when download is in progress_

info.name: GitHub Start a Pre-receive Environment Download

params.name: pre_receive_environment_id
params.description: The unique identifier of the pre-receive environment.

items.docs:
Triggers a new download of the environment tarball from the environment's `image_url`. When the download is finished, the newly downloaded tarball will overwrite the existing environment.

If a download cannot be triggered, you will receive a `422 Unprocessable Entity` response.

The possible error messages are:

* _Cannot modify or delete the default environment_
* _Can not start a new download when a download is in progress_

info.name: GitHub Create a Registration Token for an Enterprise

params.name: enterprise
params.description: The slug version of the enterprise name. You can also substitute this value with the enterprise id.

items.docs:
Returns a token that you can pass to the `config` script. The token expires after one hour.

Example using registration token:

Configure your self-hosted runner, replacing `TOKEN` with the registration token provided by this endpoint.

```
./config.sh --url https://github.com/enterprises/octo-enterprise --token TOKEN
```

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `manage_runners:enterprise` scope to use this endpoint.

info.name: GitHub Create a Remove Token for an Enterprise

params.name: enterprise
params.description: The slug version of the enterprise name. You can also substitute this value with the enterprise id.

items.docs:
Returns a token that you can pass to the `config` script to remove a self-hosted runner from an enterprise. The token expires after one hour.

Example using remove token:

To remove your self-hosted runner from an enterprise, replace `TOKEN` with the remove token provided by this
endpoint.

```
./config.sh remove --token TOKEN
```

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `manage_runners:enterprise` scope to use this endpoint.

info.name: GitHub Get the Audit Log for an Enterprise

params.name: enterprise
params.description: The slug version of the enterprise name. You can also substitute this value with the enterprise id.

params.name: phrase
params.description: A search phrase. For more information, see [Searching the audit log](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.9/admin/monitoring-activity-in-your-enterprise/reviewing-audit-logs-for-your-enterprise/searching-the-audit-log-for-your-enterprise#searching-the-audit-log).

params.name: include
params.description:
The event types to include:

- `web` - returns web (non-Git) events.
- `git` - returns Git events.
- `all` - returns both web and Git events.

The default is `web`.

params.name: after
params.description: A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.9/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for events after this cursor.

params.name: before
params.description: A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.9/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for events before this cursor.

params.name: order
params.description:
The order of audit log events. To list newest events first, specify `desc`. To list oldest events first, specify `asc`.

The default is `desc`.

params.name: page
params.description: The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.9/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

info.name: GitHub Get the Configuration Status

items.docs:
This endpoint allows you to check the status of the most recent configuration process:

Note that you may need to wait several seconds after you start a process before you can check its status.

The different statuses are:

| Status        | Description                       |
| - |  |
| `PENDING`     | The job has not started yet       |
| `CONFIGURING` | The job is running                |
| `DONE`        | The job has finished correctly    |
| `FAILED`      | The job has finished unexpectedly
